passages.text: It’s my loss, my misfortune, that I’ve become dissatisfied, with lust infecting my mind. How is it possible for someone else to dispel my discontent and give rise to satisfaction? Why don’t I do it myself?
passages.note: taking responsibility for one's own discontent

passages.text: Whatever here is included in form—on earth, in the sky, or in planet’s deep—wears out, it is all impermanent: the self-examined live having comprehended this.
passages.note: everything wears out; living with impermanence

passages.text: “I’ve got a burning desire for pleasure; My mind is on fire! Please, out of compassion, Gotama, tell me how to quench the flames.” “Your mind is on fire because of a perversion of perception. Turn away from the feature of things that’s attractive, provoking lust.

“Speak only those words that do not hurt yourself nor harm others; such speech is truly well spoken. Speak only pleasing words, words gladly welcomed. Pleasing words are those that bring nothing bad to others. Truth itself is undying speech: this is an ancient teaching. Good people say the teaching and meaning are grounded in truth.
